source.title: Sandwich Batch Normalization: A Drop-In Replacement for Feature Distribution Heterogeneity
source.authors: Xinyu Gong; Wu-Yang Chen; Tian-Long Chen; Zhang-Yang Wang

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper, including references.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports training and optimization outcomes for GANs and other applications, but it does not test whether randomly initialized classification networks reach near-zero training classification error, whether width avoids bad minima, or the initialization, depth, learning-rate, or batch-normalization claims in the listed versions.
record.gate_note: No reported result directly measures a listed claim version. Training loss, generation quality, NAS search accuracy, adversarial accuracy, and style-transfer losses concern different tasks or outcomes; no rows are included for them.
record.test_reason: The study uses batch normalization and proposes variants, reporting their application performance. It does not compare BN with no normalization for accuracy gain speed or learning-rate tolerance, and its results do not test V1–V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that SaBN and its variants improve conditional image generation, architecture search, adversarial robustness, and arbitrary style transfer by addressing model and data heterogeneity.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates a modified normalization layer in application tasks; it does not reproduce the methods or measurements in the listed claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: SaBN produces more balanced inter-class gradient magnitudes and more diverse gradient directions than CCBN in SNGAN, with lower generator loss and improved generation metrics.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adding a shared affine layer to conditional BN can improve conditional GAN optimization and image quality.

fits_no_version.finding: DARTS-SaBN improves the benchmark test accuracy of selected architectures relative to DARTS and its normalization ablations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Shared and conditional affine layers can improve architecture selection in weight-sharing NAS.

fits_no_version.finding: SaAuxBN improves clean and adversarial testing outcomes relative to AuxBN; SaAdaIN lowers training and validation content and style losses relative to AdaIN and ILM+IN.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Shared affine transformations can improve application outcomes when normalization must accommodate heterogeneous features.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Workshop/Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision
record.problems: The study reports some outcomes only as plots, but this does not affect extraction for the listed versions because none is tested.
record.rows_left_out: Application results on GAN image quality and generator loss, NAS benchmark accuracy, adversarial accuracy, and style-transfer loss are outside the listed claim versions and are not catalog rows.

untested.parts: Training classification error under the stated dataset, label corruption, capacity, and training conditions.
Spurious local minima and extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training degradation with depth, identity shortcuts, and the special initialization exceptions.
Initialization effects on learning speed, signal propagation, and trainable depth.
Loss and curvature dynamics relative to learning-rate stability thresholds.
BN versus no normalization for training speed and learning-rate tolerance; Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: Keeping the result rows empty is appropriate for these claim versions. Gradient balance, application losses, and final testing accuracy do not establish BN's training-speed advantage. The related-work discussion cites that advantage without testing it.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 under the stated network, label, size, and training-duration conditions.
Spurious minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and the effect of student width.
Depth-dependent training error in plain versus residual classification networks, and the stated special initialization and no-normalization cases.
Activation-matched, orthogonal, and convolutional initialization effects on plain-network learning speed or trainable depth.
Training-loss and curvature behavior around learning-rate stability limits.
Whether batch normalization speeds classification accuracy gains or increases learning-rate tolerance, including the Fixup comparison.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: Comparisons concern normalization variants, gradient balance, generation quality, architecture search, robustness and style transfer. They do not compare BN against no normalization for training speed or learning-rate tolerance.

tranche.reason: The study builds on normalization and reports SaBN variants' application performance; its results do not test V1–V6.

source_check.notes: The authors' conclusion is accurately paraphrased. Sections 3.1 and 5.2 discuss optimization improvements, but these do not measure any listed claim version.
